Time: 2 min. Teaching intent: Open the hour and connect it to the week's decision.
Talk track: Write an intended-use claim with evidence and explicit limits for an InPack.AI course case.
Expected answer / misconception: Students can name the outcome.
Visual: The visual previews the physical design or evidence chain.
[Sources]
R5: NIST, Digital Twins for Advanced Manufacturing | https://www.nist.gov/publications/digital-twins-advanced-manufacturing-standardized-approach

R8: IEEE TCPMT, Simulation and Experimental Study of Fan-Out Warpage | https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8590768

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Set the evidence contract.
Talk track: A credibility card with versioned inputs, reference data, residuals, and a next validation test.
Expected answer / misconception: A named artifact with source and a check, not an unsupported opinion.
Visual: Input, reasoning, and evidence are separate.
[Sources]
R5: NIST, Digital Twins for Advanced Manufacturing | https://www.nist.gov/publications/digital-twins-advanced-manufacturing-standardized-approach

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: Why is 'accurate digital twin' too broad?
Expected answer / misconception: It lacks a quantity, condition, tolerance, and intended decision.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A credibility card begins with a narrow question such as ranking two candidate layouts at one process stage. Trace the visual in order: quantity; condition; decision. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: State 'compare post-reflow warpage at 25 °C' rather than 'predict package reliability'; name the package and output definition.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: State 'compare post-reflow warpage at 25 °C' rather than 'predict package reliability'; name the package and output definition. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. 
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: Every model output and reference measurement needs a case ID, units, temperature, stage, location, and version. Trace the visual in order: case revision; output definition; reference record. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: If the classroom export omits a boundary condition, mark it missing; do not fill it from the public warpage paper.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Pause for an individual answer, then reveal and discuss.
Talk track: May the published paper supply our missing case input?
Expected answer / misconception: Only if it is explicitly the same case and justified; otherwise no.
Visual: The diagram lists the conditions to inspect without marking the answer.

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: The pattern of prediction minus measurement across cases can reveal a missing mechanism or measurement bias. Trace the visual in order: matched pairs; signed residuals; failure pattern. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: A synthetic teaching table has residuals +12, +4, -2 µm. Check stage and temperature before summarizing; do not call this InPack.AI evidence. Boundary: The residuals are synthetic classroom numbers.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Pause for an individual answer, then reveal and discuss.
Talk track: Could a low mean residual hide large individual errors?
Expected answer / misconception: Yes. Signed errors can cancel, so inspect each case and absolute error.
Visual: The diagram lists the conditions to inspect without marking the answer.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A good next test is small enough to run and specific enough to change the decision if it fails. Trace the visual in order: uncertain claim; test condition; reversal rule. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: If ranking depends on EMC CTE, test coupons or measure warpage at two temperatures bracketing the expected transition.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
